newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Damaged Russian yacht seeks help in Antarctic.
newsitem.headline: Damaged Russian yacht seeks help in Antarctic.

text.p: The crew of a Russian cruise yacht circling the globe has sought help while navigating the Southern Ocean near Antarctica, officials at Russia's Arctic-Antarctic Institute said on Monday.

Vyacheslav Martyanov, deputy head of Russian Antarctic Expeditions, said the 12-strong crew of the Apostle Andrei had requested help on Sunday in a telegram to a Russian observatory in Antarctica but had not sent an SOS distress signal.
"We lost the rudder, need someone's help. Everyone is alive," Martyanov quoted the telegram as saying, adding that the crew would have sent a real distress signal if it had faced a serious danger.
"They also asked to send the Russian scientific ship Akademik Fyodorov to rescue them, but it will take Fyodorov 12 days to reach the yacht," Martyanov told Reuters.
He added that help was more likely to come from the French Kerguelen island, which is much closer than the Russian ship at a distance which could be covered in two days.
"The Russian emergencies ministry is now checking the possibility of seeking French help," Martyanov said.

The Apostle Andrei belongs to Adventure, a Moscow travel club headed by traveller Dmitry Shparo, himself rescued from an ice-floe in the Bering Strait in March while trying to ski across the strait with his two sons.
